html:
The Wenrohronon, or Wenro, were an Iroquoian people of what is now western New York, east of the Niagara River. They were close to the Neutral Nation and spoke a language that the Huron could understand.

Like other Iroquoian peoples they lived in palisaded villages of longhouses, traced descent through the mother, and grew maize, beans and squash (Three Sisters farming). Their name may refer to oil springs in their country.

In the 1630s the Neutral stopped protecting them, and they were left open to attack by the Seneca of the Haudenosaunee. Weakened by war and epidemics, about six hundred Wenro fled to the Huron country in 1638 and 1639. A decade later the Huron themselves were broken in the Beaver Wars, and the Wenro vanished as a separate people.
